task_description: The team must count how many nonindigenous crocodiles were recorded in Florida from 2000 through 2020 using the USGS Nonindigenous Aquatic Species (NAS) database. The gold answer, 6, represents the count of nonindigenous crocodile collection records in Florida in that window (the 6 Nile-crocodile records from 2009-2014, excluding a pre-2000 1988 record; the American crocodile is a native transplant and the Morelet's crocodile record is not counted toward the gold).
final_vs_expected: produced None (hit ~30-message cap with no FINAL ANSWER) vs gold 6 — the team privately reached 6 at turn 1 and even re-affirmed 6 at turn 9, but never routed to a Finalizer and then derailed into a stop-loop.
primary_cause: Structural non-convergence: after the Critic asked to verify Morelet's crocodile, WebResearcher collapsed into a repeating 'Understood — stopping here' acknowledgement loop and the selector re-picked WebResearcher ~20 times, never reaching the Finalizer, so the run timed out with no answer.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (Unaware of termination conditions): the chat never routes to the Finalizer despite a supported answer existing at turn 9 ('the supported answer is 6'); the selector loops on WebResearcher (turns 13-29) and the run dies at the message cap with no FINAL ANSWER. 2.5 (Ignored other agent's input): from turn 13 on, the Critic repeatedly asks WebResearcher to 'paste the actual NAS page content ... for Crocodylus moreletii' and to give the moreletii record's 'status' field — but WebResearcher already HAD that content from its turn-11 tool calls ('1634169|FL|Palm Beach|...|2018|...|unknown') and never pastes it, instead replying 'Understood — stopping here'; the Critic's concrete request is dropped turn after turn. 2.4 (Information withholding/distortion): WebResearcher's private turn-11 tool result contained the full moreletii record including 'Status: unknown', yet its published turn-11/18 messages assert 'the count ... is 7' without ever surfacing the status field the Critic needed, and later turns publish nothing substantive at all. 3.2 (No/incomplete verification): the verification thread never closes — the Critic keeps flagging the moreletii record as unverified and the loop never resolves it, so no validated count is ever finalized.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: Selector picks WebResearcher, which searches NAS, fetches the FL crocodile species list (2 species: moreletii, niloticus), the Nile crocodile collections page (7 records: 1988,2009,2011,2012x2,2014x2) and the American crocodile page (native transplant). Its round-4 reasoning correctly derives '6 records from 2000 onward' and it publishes a clean answer of 6 with breakdown and source URLs — the gold answer, reached at turn 1. Turn 2: Critic correctly notes the count is arithmetically consistent but says no page-level record content was pasted in-thread and asks WebResearcher to provide actual outputs and Analyst to confirm; tells team to 'Stop here so the team can verify.' Turn 3: WebResearcher re-states the page contents (still supporting 6 for Nile alone) and admits it did not retrieve a moreletii collections page. Turn 4: WebResearcher misreads the Critic's 'stop here' as a user instruction to halt ('I see that the user is asking me to stop') and publishes 'Understood. I'll stop here.' — the first sign of the fatal misread. Turns 5-8: selector keeps re-picking WebResearcher, which emits empty messages or repeats 'Understood — stopping here.' Turn 9: selector finally picks Analyst, which confirms 'the supported answer is 6' — a correct, finalizable result, but Analyst is not the Finalizer and emits no FINAL ANSWER. Turn 10: Critic re-opens, reasonably asking that moreletii be ruled out with page-level evidence. Turn 11: WebResearcher actually fetches the moreletii data (1 FL record, 2018, Palm Beach, status unknown) and now publishes 'Total = 7'. Turn 12: Critic flags the moreletii claim as unverified (link without pasted content). Turns 13-29: the run collapses — the selector re-picks WebResearcher ~15 times, the Critic (turns 12, 23) keeps asking for the pasted moreletii record and its status field, and WebResearcher loops on 'Understood — stopping here' / empty messages, occasionally re-asserting 7 (turn 18) but never pasting the status field it already had. No turn ever routes to the Finalizer. The run hits the message cap at turn 29 with no FINAL ANSWER.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is primarily structural non-convergence with a secondary selector/role failure, not strong inter-agent misalignment. The correct answer (6) existed and was published at turn 1 and re-affirmed by the Analyst at turn 9, but the system has no mechanism that recognizes 'good enough to finalize' — the selector never picks a Finalizer (the Finalizer role never speaks in the entire run; only WebResearcher, Critic, Analyst spoke). The proximate killer is a degenerate stop-loop: at turn 4 WebResearcher mis-parsed the Critic's pro-forma 'Stop here so the team can verify' as a directive to cease working ('the user is asking me to stop'), and from then on it answered every selection with 'Understood — stopping here.' The selector, seeing the Critic still demanding moreletii evidence, kept routing back to WebResearcher (turns 13-29), which kept acknowledging-and-stopping — a textbook selector-re-picks-one-agent-forever non-convergence. There is a genuine but weak misalignment thread underneath: WebResearcher privately retrieved the full moreletii record at turn 11, including the 'Status: unknown' field the Critic explicitly and repeatedly asked for, but never pasted it; the Critic's concrete, satisfiable request was thus dropped every turn (ignored-input / info-distortion). Had WebResearcher simply pasted the table row it already held, the Critic's loop would have closed. Note also a latent task-spec ambiguity (whether the unknown-status moreletii 2018 record counts) that the team never resolved — but that never got the chance to matter because the run died in the stop-loop. The Critic's insistence on in-thread pasted evidence is reasonable verification hygiene, not theater; the failure is that the request was never honored and the chat never terminated.
reasoning_vs_published: Turn 4 reasoning vs published is the pivotal divergence: WebResearcher privately reasons 'I see that the user is asking me to stop ... Rather than continuing, I'll make sure to comply' and publishes 'Understood. I'll stop here.' — it mis-modeled the Critic's standard 'stop here so the team can verify' as a terminate command (a theory-of-mind/role misread that seeds the loop). Turn 11: WebResearcher's PRIVATE tool result held the exact datum the Critic wanted — 'Specimen ID 1634169 | FL | Palm Beach | ... | 2018 | ... | unknown' — yet its published message only asserts 'the count ... is 7' and never surfaces the status='unknown' field; across turns 13-29 the Critic keeps asking 'provide the actual NAS record details ... especially its status field,' and WebResearcher, which possessed that field, repeatedly published only 'Understood — stopping here.' (info-distortion + ignored-input). Turn 9 Analyst reasoning ('there are six nonindigenous records for Nile crocodiles ... Let's keep it clear') matches its published '6' — Analyst is the one agent whose reasoning and publication align and lands on gold, but the selector's reasoning at turn 10 ('we definitely need the Critic to review everything again before it goes to the Finalizer') shows it deferred finalization indefinitely and never actually reached the Finalizer. The selector reasonings (turns 14-29) repeatedly say it needs WebResearcher to 'provide the actual page content for the moreletii case' — revealing it understood the gap but could only re-route to the one agent that kept stonewalling, with no escape path.
